help.title: Help
help.intro: Kukátko is your photo gallery – a place to find, organise and rediscover your photos and videos. Below is a short tour of what the app does and how each feature behaves. What exactly you can do depends on your role (see the User roles section).

browsing.title: Browsing photos
browsing.body:
The home page is your library – every photo newest-first, with endless scrolling. In the filters you choose how many tiles fit on a row (the “Tiles per row” control), so you can go from large previews to a dense grid. Click a photo to open it full-screen, where you'll see its details and more actions.
The app remembers your browsing state: the filters and sorting in the page address, so you can share a link to the current view, and how far you had scrolled for the length of your visit – so Back (and the viewer's “Back to list”) returns you exactly where you left off.

search.title: Search
search.body:
The search field above the library matches photo titles, descriptions and notes – and it also understands the “key:value” filters, exactly like full search: “year:1965” narrows the library to 1965, “person:Jarmila” to photos of Jarmila. The “?” beside the field lists every filter, and so does the table further down this chapter. A filter we did not understand is pointed out rather than left as an empty library. Full search (from the search bar at the top or the “/” key) can also search by content: type what should be in the photo and Kukátko finds visually matching shots, even when nothing is written about them.
Search by content depends on the AI service. When it happens to be offline, ordinary search by title and description keeps working.
search.queryIntro: Besides words, the search field takes filters in the form key:value. A few ready-made queries to copy:

example.person: Photos of Jarmila you rated four or five stars.
example.album: Photos from the Léto 2024 album with at least two faces.

albums.title: Albums
albums.body: Albums group photos that belong together by hand – a trip, a party, a year. Add a photo to an album from its detail view or in bulk from a selection in the library. The “Expand” tool then finds more similar photos across the whole library, so nothing gets left out. Albums are managed by editors.

labels.title: Labels
labels.body: Labels (tags) describe what's in a photo – “sunset”, “dog”, “family”. A photo can have several, and they make filtering and searching quick. Adding and managing labels is for editors; labels also support “Expand”, which finds more photos a label would suit.

favorites.title: Favourites & ratings
favorites.body: The heart on a photo adds it to your favourites, and the stars give it a rating. Favourites and ratings are personal – everyone has their own, and they don't see or affect each other. You can then easily show just what you marked yourself.

people.title: People & faces
people.body:
Kukátko finds faces in your photos on its own. Assign a face to a person and from then on the app suggests where else they might appear (“this person may also be here”) by visual similarity – you just confirm suggestions instead of searching by hand.
Sorting is a one-question game: the app asks “Is this Jane?” and you answer Yes, No, or Not sure. That way you get through a big pile fast and without overthinking. The leaderboard shows who sorted the most – every Yes and No earns you a point.
When something goes wrong it's easy to fix: reassign a face to a different person or remove the assignment. The “Possible mistakes” section flags faces that probably don't belong to a given person.

duplicates.title: Duplicates
duplicates.body: Kukátko can find near-identical photos – the same shot uploaded more than once, or small variations. You compare a group of duplicates side by side and merge them: one photo stays and the rest are tidied away, with albums, labels and assigned people carried over to the one you keep. Merging is done by editors.

stacks.title: Variants of one shot
stacks.body: A stack groups variants of the same shot – for example a RAW and a JPEG from one press of the shutter, or an edited version next to the original – under a single photo. So you don't see almost the same thing five times in the library; the variants stay together and you pick one as the main one. Nothing is deleted, it is only grouped.

map.title: Map & places
map.body: Photos with location data appear on a map, so you can see where you took them. The Places section then groups them by country and city. For some photos Kukátko estimates the location from other shots taken nearby at the same time – such a value is always marked as an estimate.

deleting.title: Deleting & the trash
deleting.body:
Deleting has two steps. Archiving is reversible – the photo moves to the trash and you can restore it any time. Permanent deletion removes the photo for good. Archived photos are also removed from the trash automatically once the retention period passes, so the trash keeps itself tidy.
Permanent deletion and emptying the trash are reserved for admins.

sharing.title: Adding photos from your phone
sharing.body:
On Android it works straight from the gallery: pick the photos, tap Share and choose Kukátko. The app opens on the upload page with those files already queued — look them over, give the batch an album and labels if you like, and upload as usual. The one condition is that Kukátko is added to the home screen (installed); otherwise it does not appear in the share sheet.
iPhone cannot do this yet — Safari has no support for sharing into web apps, and there is no honest way to fake it. Add photos on the upload page instead: the Choose files button opens the photo library, or copy a photo in Photos and paste it here. Adding Kukátko to the home screen still pays off: it then opens straight away, even with no signal.
Uploading needs the editor role or higher. A view-only account is told why its shared photos were not added. Only photos and videos can be shared; anything else is left out and listed on the page.

import.title: Importing the library
import.body: Photos come into Kukátko by importing from your existing library. The import is incremental and non-destructive – it only adds new items and never touches the originals. It is run by maintainers.

roles.title: User roles
roles.body: What you can do in Kukátko depends on your role. Roles form a ladder – each higher one can do everything the one below can, plus more:
roles.viewer: Views photos, albums, labels, the map and the leaderboard. Changes nothing.
roles.editor: Additionally edits photos and their details, sorts faces, and manages albums and labels.
roles.admin: Additionally manages users, sees the audit log, and can delete permanently.
roles.maintainer: Additionally runs imports and maintenance, watches system status, and manages backups.

account.title: Your account
account.body: In My account (in the menu at the top right under your name) you change your password, switch the app language, and see your role. It is also where you can check whether the app is running fine.

apiTokens.title: API tokens
apiTokens.body:
An API token is a password for programs. When you want a script of yours, the kukatko ctl command line or some helper to reach Kukátko, you create a token for it instead of handing over your password.
Tokens live in My account → API tokens. The secret is shown exactly once, right when the token is created — copy it and keep it somewhere safe, because nobody can show it again. A token carries exactly your own permissions, so treat it like a password. When you no longer need it, or it ended up in the wrong hands, revoke it: it stops working at once.

help.title: Search query language
help.intro: Mix free text with key:value filters in one query. An unknown filter does no harm — it is searched as plain text and the search points it out.
help.example: dovolená camera:"Canon EOS R6" iso:100-400 faces:2

op.and: A space between filters means AND.
op.or: A pipe inside a value means OR.
op.not: An exclamation mark negates a value (photos without the label).
op.notText: A minus before a word excludes free text.
op.range: Ranges with a dash; either side may be open.
op.quotes: Quotes for values with spaces; \ escapes |, ! and -.
op.wildcard: An asterisk is a wildcard inside a text value.

desc.text: The photo's title, description and notes.
desc.photoText: Text read out of the photo itself (a sign, a shop front, a scanned page). Accents are ignored — the recogniser often loses them.
desc.album: Photos in an album (by title or UID).
desc.label: Photos carrying a label (by name or UID).
desc.person: Photos with a person (by name or UID). `person:me` is the person that is you, as set on My account.
desc.uploader: Who uploaded the photo (by username or account name, accents ignored). `uploader:me` is you, `uploader:none` are the imported photos.
desc.hidden: Hidden from the library (yes/no) — the way back to a hidden photo.
desc.flag: Your mark: pick (picked), reject (rejected) or eye (to look at later).
desc.takenAdded: Capture date / date added to the catalogue: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.
desc.dated: Photos with a capture date, or without one. `dated:no` is the worklist of everything undated — including what never had a date at all.
desc.beforeAfter: Taken before a date / on or after a date.
desc.geo: Photos with GPS coordinates, or without them.
desc.near: Photos geographically near the given photo; dist: is the km radius (default 5).
desc.camera: Camera make or model, and the lens.
desc.optics: ISO, aperture, focal length in mm and megapixels.
desc.type: Media type: image, video or live.
desc.faces: Face count (faces:3 = at least three); face:new = a face nobody named yet.
desc.uid: One photo by its own ID (or by the source ID it was imported under). It finds it even when archived or hidden.

search.personMeUnlinked: The person:me filter looks for the person that is you — and your account has not said which person that is, so it found nothing.

via.photoprism: the photo imported under that source ID

scan.summary: {{photos}} photos · {{files}} files in the catalogue · {{disk}} originals on disk
scan.summaryHint: These numbers should roughly agree. A bigger gap between the catalogue and the disk means something drifted apart — either a photo’s original is gone (it is in the catalogue but not on disk), or a file sits on disk that the catalogue knows nothing about. See below.

descriptions.missing_originals: The photo is in the catalogue, but its original file is neither on disk nor in storage. This one is a real risk of loss and deserves attention.
descriptions.orphan_files: The file sits in storage but belongs to no photo in the catalogue — it was never imported. The “Add the files the catalogue is missing” repair takes it in.
descriptions.missing_thumbnails: The photo has no small copy for the grid, so it may load slowly or stay blank. The thumbnail repair fixes it.
descriptions.missing_embeddings: Kukátko has not yet worked out what is in the photo, so searching by content — and finding similar photos — will not turn it up. It is filled in once the recognition service is available.
descriptions.missing_faces: Nobody has looked for faces in this photo yet, so it will not show up under people. It is filled in once the recognition service is available.
descriptions.missing_phashes: The photo has no short fingerprint of how it looks; that is what near-identical copies are found by.

jobs.title: Background work

nameless.title: The nameless person (an import catch-all)
nameless.hint: A person with no name cannot be created by hand — an import minted one as a catch-all and every unnamed face after it landed on them. They tend to sit first in the list of people and they are not a real person. The check changes nothing; detaching cannot be undone, so it always hands you a file to undo it with first.

descriptions.total: Everything Kukátko has on record, finished work included.
descriptions.queued: Waiting its turn — including work scheduled for another attempt and work put aside until the recognition service is back (waiting costs it no attempts).
descriptions.failed: Something that makes no sense to retry (usually 0 — ordinary errors are retried and end up under “permanently failed” if they keep going wrong).
descriptions.dead: It went wrong even after several attempts (five by default), so Kukátko set it aside. It will not try again on its own — send it back to the queue with the “Retry the permanently failed” button on the System status page. A high number usually means something keeps going wrong, or that the recognition service was unavailable for a long time.
descriptions.pending: Work for the recognition service (reading what is in a photo and finding faces) that is waiting for the service to come back.
descriptions.done: Finished successfully. It stays on record, which is why one kind of work can total far more than the number of photos it ever touched.

errors.accountBlocked: The account is blocked. Enable it first, then try again.
errors.notAllowed: You may not manage this account. Only a system maintainer can manage a maintainer account.
errors.gone: The account no longer exists. Reload the list.

email.noneHint: A placeholder address — nothing sent to it can arrive. Fill in a real one.

approve.title: Approve the account?
approve.body: {{username}} will be able to sign in and will get an e-mail about it. The role does not change — you set that separately.
approve.blockedHint: A blocked account cannot be approved. Enable it first.

resetLink.title: Issue a password link for {{username}}?
resetLink.body: {{username}} gets a one-time link by e-mail and chooses a new password themselves. The current password keeps working until they do. Any earlier unused link of this account stops working.
resetLink.mailed: The link was e-mailed to {{email}} and is valid for {{days}} days.
resetLink.notMailed: The account has no real e-mail address, so nothing was sent — pass the link on yourself. It is valid for {{days}} days.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.subtitle: A durable record of changes on this instance, newest first. Filter by actor, action, entity or date.
audit.adminOnly: This page is available to administrators only.
audit.error: The audit log could not be loaded.

empty.title: No entries
empty.hint: No events match the current filters. Try relaxing them.

details.moreLinks: The rest ({{n}}) is in the payload below.

expand.title: Expand a collection
expand.subtitle: Find photos that look like the ones already in an album or on a label, and add them in one step.

form.sourcesError: Albums and labels failed to load.

error.search: The similarity search failed. Please try again.
error.reject: The rejection could not be saved; the photo stays in the results.

idle.title: Pick a collection to expand
idle.hint: Choose an album or a label and Kukátko finds photos that look like its current members — ready to be added.

noEmbeddings.title: The collection's photos have no embeddings yet
noEmbeddings.hint: The collection has photos, but none of them has an embedding computed yet. Embeddings are computed while the compute box is online — try again later.

emptyCollection.title: The collection is empty
emptyCollection.hint: The chosen album or label holds no photos, so there is nothing to be similar to.

noResults.title: No similar photos
noResults.hint: Nothing cleared the similarity threshold. Try lowering it and searching again.

summary.sampled: A sample of {{sampled}} of {{count}} source photos was used.
summary.voteRule_one: A photo must match at least {{count}} source photo.
summary.voteRule_other: A photo must match at least {{count}} source photos.
summary.ordering: Sorted by match count, then by similarity.
summary.allHandled: Every found photo has been handled — run the search again for more.

question.label: Does the label {{name}} fit this photo?

review.faceHint: The face under review is highlighted with a frame.
review.openPhoto: Open the photo in a new tab

empty.libraryHint: There are no named people or labels yet to build questions from.
empty.queueHint: No questions right now. New ones appear as photos or suggestions arrive.
empty.noPeopleHint: The game is asking about people only, but nobody is named yet. Name someone, or switch to labels.
empty.noLabelsHint: The game is asking about labels only, but no label has photos yet — or they are all switched off for the game on the Labels page. Create a label, switch one back on, or ask about people.
empty.queueHintScoped: Nothing left to sort in the chosen source. Try asking about both, or come back later.

errors.load: The question queue failed to load.
errors.undo: The answer could not be undone.

duplicate.hint: Compare the two side by side. Nothing is merged — we only record what you think.

outlier.hint: The face crop, with the whole photo beside it for context.
outlier.contextAlt: The whole photo the face is on

place.hint: We guessed the place from photos taken nearby in time.

review.comboTitle: How many answers you have in a row. A skip breaks the run.
review.streakTitle_one: {{count}} day in a row with an answer
review.streakTitle_other: {{count}} days in a row with an answer

breather.joy: just for the joy of it
breather.favorite: Somebody has this photo in their favourites.

compose.title: Announcement
compose.intro: Publish a short message shown as a banner at the top of the app to every signed-in user (for example planned downtime).

person.hint: Pick the person in the library that is you. The app can then show you the photos you are on, and person:me starts working in search. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
person.publishWarning: Note: once you pick a person, their profile photo will appear next to every comment you write — everyone who opens the photo will see it.
person.empty: Nobody in the library has been named yet.
person.unknownPerson: The linked person is no longer in the library.
person.error: Could not save the link. Please try again.

pwa.offline: You are offline. Kukátko opens, but photos and the library need a connection.

update.message: A new version of Kukátko is available.
